newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state Hesse February CPI up 0.3 pct mth-mth.
newsitem.headline: German state Hesse February CPI up 0.3 pct mth-mth.

text.p: The German state of Hesse said on Tuesday that consumer prices in February rose 0.3 percent month-on-month and rose 1.5 percent over February 1996.
In January, the state of Hesse said prices rose 0.4 percent month-on-month and were up 1.6 percent year-on-year.

The state said prices developed similarly in February as in recent months and noted that prices rose sharply over February 1996 levels for heating oil, which was up 12 percent, and for natural gas at 5.5 percent.
Price declines were reported for food products such as potatoes, coffee, butter, cheese as well as for televisions.
The state of Hesse was the first of the four states to report on consumer prices for the month. Data from the four states is used to compute provisional west German consumer prices.
